messages.subject: P-card and T-card basics for department staff
messages.body:
Hello all,

A refresher on the two cards.

P-card (procurement card): supplies, registrations, software under $5,000, and visitor parking for guests of the department. Put the visitor's name and the business purpose in the memo line.

T-card (travel card): airfare, hotels, and ground transport while an employee is on university travel. Parking at the airport or at a conference hotel goes on the T-card.

Receipts for both cards are uploaded in the expense system.

Finance Office

messages.subject: Update: visitor parking validations move to the Parking Services portal
messages.body:
Hello all,

Starting October 1, 2026, visitor parking is no longer an allowable P-card purchase.

Buy visitor parking validations in the Parking Services portal (parking.example.edu/validations). Charge them to your department SpeedType; the portal asks for it at checkout. One validation covers one vehicle for one day in the visitor lots.

The T-card is unchanged: it covers an employee's own parking while on university travel, never a visitor's.

The attached guide has screenshots.

Finance Office

messages.subject: RE: Parking for Friday's seminar speaker?
messages.body:
Hi Dana,

Not the P-card any more. Buy a validation in the Parking Services portal and charge it to SpeedType 1234567. Finance sent the new rule on September 15; the PDF on that email has the screenshots.

Best,
Me

messages.subject: Reminder: T-card receipts are due within 30 days
messages.body:
Reminder: every T-card charge needs its receipt uploaded in the expense system within 30 days of the trip's end. Charges without receipts after 60 days are deducted from the traveler's pay.
